claim_comment: Validating the committed-observation contract against the accepted capability registry and handshake: retry-safe idempotency, exact repository/worktree/session scope, explicit unknown-extension handling, and a strict distinction between an observation and provider-created memory state.
acceptance_criteria: Retrying the same observation cannot create a second effect.
Repository/worktree/session scope is mandatory for coding observations.
Unknown extensions are preserved or explicitly rejected.
The contract distinguishes observation from resulting memory records.
close_reason: Accepted the V1 committed-observation and idempotency contract with exact coding scope, explicit extension behavior, and no one-observation/one-memory-record assumption.
close_comment: Evidence: the versioned observation contract, strict schema, repository validator, documentation, and mutation tests define immutable post-settlement observations with deterministic canonical payloads and idempotency keys, mandatory exact repository/worktree/session scope, source settlement and provenance/privacy metadata, bounded at-least-once delivery, duplicate/out-of-order tolerance, explicit opaque-preserve-or-typed-reject extension behavior, and provider receipts that distinguish observation acceptance from arbitrary provider-local memory encoding. Same key plus same payload is duplicate acknowledgement; the same key plus a different payload is an idempotency conflict. Provider admission or delivery cannot alter the settled TraceDecay source outcome or observer-mode product output.
